title: Buy Land and Build, or Buy a Ready-Built House? Cost, Time and Risk
desc: Buy land and build, or buy a finished house? A comparison of costs, time, procedures, legal risks, quality and the expenses to budget for under each option.
summary: A comparison of buying land to build versus buying an existing house in terms of cost, time, procedures and risk, with a list of expenses to budget for.
body: p

With the same amount of money, many families hesitate between buying land and building and buying a ready-built house. There is no right choice for everyone; this article helps you compare them on one table before deciding.
h2
1. Quick comparison of the two options
ul
Time: a ready-built house can be occupied right after the title transfer; buying land to build takes extra time for design, permit, construction and as-built completion (hoàn công).
Quality: building yourself lets you control the design, materials and workmanship; with an existing house it is hard to know the foundations, reinforcement and internal waterproofing.
Functionality: building yourself follows the family's needs; with an existing house you usually have to accept it or alter it.
Cash flow: buying land can be split into stages (buy the land first, save up, then build); an existing house needs the full amount at once (or a single loan).
Effort: building yourself requires time for monitoring and choosing a contractor; an existing house is simpler.
h2
2. Buying land to build: expenses to budget for
ol
Land price, notarisation costs and registration fee (Registration fee on houses and land 2026); personal income tax is usually paid by the seller, but the parties may agree otherwise.

Design: a small house (under 3 floors, under 250 m² of floor area, no basement, under 12 m high) may be designed under the owner's own arrangement; larger ones must hire a qualified firm (Article 10 of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP).
A construction permit if the house requires one (Article 43 of the Construction Law 2025) – see the procedure for applying for a construction permit.
Construction costs for the shell, finishing, electricity and water; supervision if hired (what a construction estimate includes).
A contingency for unforeseen costs – set aside a separate percentage (for example 10%) of the construction cost.
Rent for temporary housing during construction (if any).
h2
3. Buying a ready-built house: expenses to budget for
ol
Purchase price, notarisation, registration fee.
Costs of inspecting the condition (it is advisable to have an engineer check for cracks, damp and settlement) and of repairs and renovation after purchase.
Costs of updating the documents if extensions have not been recorded on the land use right certificate.
h2
4. Legal risks to check before paying
p

Whichever option you choose, land and houses can be transferred only if there is a certificate, no dispute, no attachment, the land use term has not expired and no interim emergency measure applies (Clause 1, Article 45 of the Land Law).
ul
Buying land to build: check the land use purpose (it must be residential land), the zoning, the building line and the minimum area permitted for construction – see how to request zoning information.
Buying an existing house: compare the actual house with the certificate and the construction permit; parts built contrary to the permit may be sanctioned.
Pay the deposit under a clear contract – see deposits for buying and selling houses and land.
h2
5. Comparison example with assumed figures
p
Suppose a family has a budget of VND 2 billion (own funds plus a loan):
ul

Option A – buy land for VND 1.2 billion + build for VND 700 million + contingency of VND 70 million: total about VND 1.97 billion, a new house to your own design, but it takes 8–12 months (assumed) and you must pay rent during that time.
Option B – buy an existing house for VND 1.8 billion + repairs of VND 150 million: total about VND 1.95 billion, move in early, but the quality of hidden parts is hard to control.
p
These figures only illustrate the method of comparison; actual land and construction prices differ by area and over time.
h2
6. Which option to choose?
ul
Choose buying land to build if: you have time to monitor the work, want a house to your own wishes and want to spread cash flow over stages.
Choose an existing house if: you need somewhere to live immediately, have no time to manage construction, and can find one with complete documents and a sound structure.
p

note
